Odin × Godot

Box3D native backend

6 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Build and useSimulation contractOwnership and identityComplete state and diagnostics

This package is the framework-independent, explicitly stepped Box3D backend shared by the separate Kit and Replay adapters. It owns native physics resources. Each adapter owns its game state, stable entity mappings, input history, transactions and presentation.

The authoritative foreign boundary is native/api.h and the additive native/motion.h, with owned snapshots and normalized state diagnostics in native/owned_snapshot.h and native/state_dump.h. The Odin declarations mirror that flat C API, not Box3D's private layouts or any C++ class. Engine and shim revisions, notices and build configuration are recorded in dependency.json and the native build metadata.

Build and use#

Build one pinned engine and shim archive, then give its absolute path to Odin:

Shell
nix develop --command bash build/build_box3d.sh Debug .box3d-cache
nix develop --command odin check box3d -no-entry-point \
  -define:BOX3D_LIBRARY="$(pwd)/.box3d-cache/build/Debug/libogb3.a"
nix develop --command bash tests/box3d/run.sh \
  "$(pwd)/.box3d-cache/build/Debug/libogb3.a"

Use Release for the optimized native build. Native assertions, validation and the floating-point policy remain enabled. BOX3D_LIBRARY defaults to native/libogb3.a relative to this package; no archive is committed. Import the package as godot:box3d with the existing repository collection, or use its local path. Linux additionally links libm. The supported initial native targets are macOS arm64 and Linux x86-64; evidence for each target is recorded separately.

Odin
world, status := box3d.world_create(box3d.world_def_default())
if status != .Ok {return}
defer box3d.world_destroy(&world)

def := box3d.body_def_default()
def.type = .Dynamic
def.pose.position = {0, 3, 0}
body, body_status := box3d.body_create(world, def)
if body_status != .Ok {return}
_, shape_status := box3d.shape_box(body, box3d.shape_def_default(), {0.5, 0.5, 0.5})
if shape_status != .Ok {return}
if box3d.world_step_fixed(world) != .Ok {return}

snapshot, capture_status := box3d.snapshot_capture(world)
if capture_status != .Ok {return}
defer box3d.snapshot_destroy(&snapshot)

Use native default constructors before changing definition fields. POD flag fields use u32 values 0/1, body kinds use Body_Type, and public body/shape/ joint mutation helpers accept Odin booleans where applicable. abi_check compares the ABI version and every POD field's offset, size and alignment with C. world_create runs it before creation. Default constructors fail loudly on an incompatible ABI before C can write to a POD.

Object operations return Status; validity queries return (bool, Status) and report stale handles as false, .Ok. Creation returns (typed_handle, Status). Read outputs only after checking status. Native wrapper allocation failures can return .Out_Of_Memory; upstream engine allocations still assert on exhaustion.

Simulation contract#

Positions use meters in a Y-up, right-handed coordinate system. Rotations use quaternions in (x, y, z, w) order. Transforms are rigid; bake scale into immutable geometry. The initial corpus uses one worker, 60 ticks per second and four substeps. Process-wide unit settings must be initialized before creating worlds. Keep engine configuration and callback identity fixed during a simulation run.

All mutation, queries, capture and restore happen at settled step boundaries on the owning thread. The package does not schedule ticks or mutate Godot scenes. Run Odin tests with -define:ODIN_TEST_THREADS=1; the supplied test script does so.

Query and sensor APIs copy results into caller-owned slices and return the total available count. .Capacity means the prefix that fits was copied; retry with enough storage for a complete result. Empty slices are valid size queries. Query order is the engine's traversal order; adapters choose any required stable game-ID ordering after copying. Ray translation is the full displacement. The hinge axis is local Z in both local frames.

The additive motion API supplies query_aabb, query_ray_sorted, query_capsule and query_capsule_cast. These gather complete bounded results, return allocation keys and sort by hit fraction and stable key/geometry ties. An undersized output returns .Capacity without publishing a partial prefix. Motion_Filter includes sensor selection and an explicit self body exclusion. The existing raw query functions retain their earlier behavior.

character_step reads the actual world and returns explicit caller-owned Character_State through Character_Result. It uses the pinned engine's capsule casts and collision-plane solver; it neither mutates a body nor steps the world. Store that value in Game/Side and call it from the existing framework tick. The accepted time step is zero or the existing fixed 1/60. See the motion contract for the distinct Kit and Replay entry points and the authored node/resource surface.

Both the sensor and convex visitor shapes must enable sensor events. This initial API supports primitive/convex sensors and static mesh collision. Mesh sensor or mesh visitor event flags return .Unsupported; the pinned engine's sensor path cannot form a convex proxy for a mesh visitor. Geometry beyond the supported surface needs explicit native support and evidence before use. Motion_Joint_Def supports Pin, Hinge, Slider, Spherical, Distance, Motor, Weld and Wheel. Pin maps to a spherical point constraint, Hinge to Revolute and Slider to Prismatic. Each definition uses world-independent body allocation keys, and creation returns a joint key. The current profile still permits one joint at a time.

Ownership and identity#

Worlds and bodies/shapes/joints use distinct typed native handles. These are runtime references, not durable game identities. Destroying a body also destroys its shapes and joints. Destroying a world invalidates all its object handles. Zero is the empty value. Destruction helpers clear the caller's owning variable after successful destruction; ordinary copies do not create another owner. World/body/shape/joint destruction returns .Invalid_Handle for an empty or stale handle. Snapshot and geometry destruction accept an empty owner.

Geometry owns copied hull points or indexed mesh vertices. Mesh indices are triangle triples. geometry_destroy releases the caller's lease, and any native shape/world ownership remains valid. Native worlds conservatively retain mesh asset leases through destroyed-shape history until world destruction; use bounded predeclared assets. Snapshot geometry metrics describe reachable retained assets, not every native/wrapper allocation.

Snapshots own their images and immutable geometry dependencies. Clone explicitly when a second history entry or checkpoint needs independent ownership, and destroy each owner once. Copying a snapshot value aliases its native owner; it does not clone. A successful restored world retains the geometry dependencies it needs independently of the snapshot that supplied them.

Restore clears process-local body/shape/joint user data and output event buffers. Adapters must reconstruct their associations from rollback-owned stable mappings. Snapshot-era handles can become valid again, and future resimulated spawns can reuse a numerical handle. A handle's value therefore does not identify a unique gameplay lifetime. Cross-world restore also requires native handle retargeting. Use body_retarget, shape_retarget and joint_retarget with snapshot-era handles and the destination world. body_identity returns native allocation index/generation without the world slot; it still is not durable game identity.

Capture physics and deterministic game state at the same tick. A physics snapshot alone does not include gameplay RNG, entity/body maps, timers, health, pending commands or framework events. Stage speculative execution in a separate world; publish physics and game state together only after all checks succeed.

Complete state and diagnostics#

The motion digest covers poses and awake velocities. It is a diagnostic only. It cannot establish complete solver equality or justify reusing a rollback suffix. The normalized solver dump/digest carries an explicit coverage/version contract; its supported coverage must be checked against the native manifest. Adapters still need to include deterministic game side-state in a complete checkpoint or comparison. Preserve normalized bytes when diagnosing mismatches.

world_dump/snapshot_dump return (required_bytes, Status). Any empty slice is a successful size query. A nonempty undersized slice returns .Capacity without writing a partial dump. world_digests/snapshot_digests return explicitly named complete_solver_digest and motion_digest fields. Snapshot diagnostics inspect its sealed captured resource directly. state_version, state_coverage and build_fingerprint describe compatibility; the fingerprint is diagnostic only.

snapshot_metrics reports image used/capacity and geometry bytes/count. Clones have independent leases on one immutable resource, so summing clone metrics can double-count shared storage. engine_allocation_stats reports process-wide engine calls/requested bytes/live/high-water bytes; it excludes wrapper mallocs and snapshot owner/normalized-dump mallocs. Neither counter set alone measures total backend memory. snapshot_storage additionally reports retained normalized bytes, wrapper malloc bytes and native requested bytes for the captured resource. These per-resource figures overlap the other counters; consult the native header before totaling them, and count shared clone storage once. snapshot_allocation_stats reports successful wrapper allocations process-wide, including temporary digest storage and branch/restore owners and leases. It uses the same Allocation_Stats fields as engine counters. Caller buffers, flat-API geometry owners and allocator overhead are excluded; these are requested-byte counters, not process resident memory.

Owned local snapshots are exact-build implementation data. They are separate from a portable, validated recovery/network codec. Passing the native ownership and ABI checks does not establish Gate A, cross-target determinism, either framework integration, or canonical transferred recovery.
